message.reasoning:
I am evaluating a trade offer to accept, reject, or counter.

I have a dark blue monopoly with no houses built. The counterparty owns red and orange properties. I am weighing whether $260 for Kentucky Avenue is worth the trade.

I will reject the offer. The $260 price is only $40 above list value, and giving up Kentucky would hand the opponent two of three red properties.

The $260 offer would raise my cash to $623. That is enough to build three houses on the dark blue monopoly. I am reconsidering whether the trade is worth it.

Building three houses evenly on the dark blue monopoly would cost $1,200. That is far beyond my available cash. Even with the $260 offer, I could only afford two houses total. The resulting rent would be too weak to block the opponent.

The opponent has $873 in cash. That is enough to buy Indiana from the first player and complete the red monopoly. A red block with houses would be devastating.

I considered countering with a trade for Illinois, but that would give me only two of three red properties and would be expensive. I do not need anything from the opponent. I will reject the offer.
